definitions.explanation: The fleshy back part of the lower leg between the knee and the ankle. Most commonly encountered in the compound こむら返り (leg cramp).

examples.english: I got a cramp in my calf.

examples.japanese: ⟦マラソン→マラソン：04732_marason⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{途中|とちゅう}→途中：01684_tochuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{腓|こむら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}く→痛い：01108_itai⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: My calf started hurting in the middle of the marathon.

examples.japanese: ⟦{泳|およ}いでいる→泳ぐ：00545_oyogu⟧とき⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{急|きゅう}→急：13042_kyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{腓|こむら}{返|がえ}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きて→起きる：00521_okiru⟧、⟦{慌|あわ}てて→慌てる：01874_awateru⟧プールサイド⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つかまった。
examples.english: I suddenly got a calf cramp while swimming and grabbed onto the pool edge in a panic.

notes:
An older anatomical term that survives mainly in the compound {腓|こむら}{返|がえ}り (calf cramp; charley horse). In modern everyday Japanese, the calf is more commonly called ⟦ふくらはぎ→ふくらはぎ：16894_fukurahagi⟧. The kanji {腓|こむら} is rarely used; the word is usually written in hiragana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {腓|こむら}{返|がえ}り: calf cramp; charley horse — by far the most common use of this word
- {腓|こむら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つる: to get a calf cramp
- {腓|こむら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{筋肉|きんにく}→筋肉：02646_kinniku⟧: calf muscle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ふくらはぎ→ふくらはぎ：16894_fukurahagi⟧: calf (of the leg) — the standard modern term, used in everyday conversation
- {脹脛|ふくらはぎ}: calf — kanji spelling of ⟦ふくらはぎ→ふくらはぎ：16894_fukurahagi⟧, rarely used

NOTE ON USAGE:
Learners are most likely to encounter this word in the expression {腓|こむら}{返|がえ}り. If you experience a sudden painful cramp in your calf — common during exercise, swimming, or while sleeping — that is {腓|こむら}{返|がえ}り.
